description: Runtime database usage patterns: connection pooling, query execution discipline, service account governance, and transaction lifecycle management. Complements data-modeling-rules.json (schema design) with operational runtime rules.

connection_pooling.description: Connection pool configuration and lifecycle — required for every service that connects to the DB

rules.description: Connection pooling must be configured — never create a new DB connection per request
rules.message: Use a connection pool (e.g., pg Pool, Kysely pool) — never create a new raw DB connection per request
rules.design_check: Does the design specify a connection pool for database access? BLOCK if the design creates a new DB connection per request or per operation with no shared pool.

rules.description: Connection pool must declare explicit min/max connection limits
rules.message: Pool must define explicit min/max connection counts — unbounded pools exhaust DB server connections under load
rules.design_check: Does the design specify explicit min and max connection counts for the pool? BLOCK if the pool is created without bounded limits (max connections unset).

rules.description: Pool must configure connection timeout and idle timeout to prevent leaks
rules.message: Configure idleTimeoutMillis and connectionTimeoutMillis on the pool to prevent silent connection leaks
rules.design_check: Does the design configure connection timeout and idle timeout for the pool? Flag if missing — connection leaks can exhaust the pool silently under sustained load.

rules.description: Do not create a new DB connection inside a request handler or middleware
rules.message: Never create a DB connection inside a request handler — acquire from a shared pool instead
rules.design_check: Does the design create or open DB connections inside request handlers, controllers, or middleware? If so, replace with pool acquisition. BLOCK.

service_accounts.description: Database service account governance — dedicated least-privilege accounts per service, never shared superuser

rules.description: Each service must use a dedicated DB account — not postgres, root, admin, or sa
rules.message: Use a dedicated service account per service — never use postgres/root/admin for application code
rules.design_check: Does the design specify dedicated DB service accounts per service (e.g., advisorapp, advisor_ai)? BLOCK if any service is configured to use postgres, root, admin, dba, or sa.

rules.description: Service accounts must receive only the minimum permissions they need per schema
rules.message: Never GRANT ALL — assign specific permissions per schema (e.g., CRUD on core, read-only on lookup, append-only on audit)
rules.design_check: Does the design grant permissions at a fine-grained level per schema (e.g., SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on core, SELECT-only on lookup)? BLOCK if GRANT ALL or blanket permissions are proposed.

rules.description: Read-only services should use a read-only DB account to limit blast radius
rules.message: Consider a read-only DB account for services that only read data — limits blast radius of a compromised credential
rules.design_check: Are there services in the design that only read data? If so, propose a read-only DB account for those services to limit the impact of a credential compromise.

rules.description: Service accounts must not share credentials across service boundaries
rules.message: Each service must have its own unique DB credentials — no shared accounts across service boundaries
rules.design_check: Does the design reuse a single DB account across multiple distinct services? If so, create separate accounts per service. BLOCK on shared credentials across service boundaries.

rules.description: Application service accounts must not have DDL permissions
rules.message: Application service accounts must not have DDL permissions (CREATE, DROP, ALTER) — schema changes belong in migrations run by a migration-only account
rules.design_check: Does the design give application service accounts DDL permissions (CREATE TABLE, DROP, ALTER)? If so, remove — DDL belongs to migration scripts run with a migration-specific account. BLOCK.

query_execution.description: Query execution discipline — safety, performance, and correctness

rules.description: All queries must use parameterized binding — no string interpolation of user input into SQL
rules.message: CRITICAL: Never interpolate variables into SQL strings — use parameterized queries ($1, ?, named params) or an ORM
rules.design_check: Does the design specify parameterized queries or ORM-based query building for all DB interactions? BLOCK if the design mentions string-concatenated or template-literal SQL with dynamic values.

rules.description: All list/collection queries must be paginated — no unbounded result sets
rules.message: All list queries must include pagination (LIMIT/OFFSET or cursor-based) — unbounded queries can OOM the server
rules.design_check: Do all list/collection queries in the design include pagination (page size, cursor, or LIMIT/OFFSET)? BLOCK if any list query is unbounded with no limit.

rules.description: Use batch operations instead of per-item queries in loops (N+1 prevention)
rules.message: Avoid querying inside loops (N+1) — use batch INSERT/UPDATE, WHERE IN (...), or JOIN instead
rules.design_check: Does the design involve processing a list and querying or updating the DB per item in a loop? If so, replace with batch operations (WHERE IN, bulk insert, JOIN). BLOCK on loop-per-query patterns.

rules.description: Repositories must list explicit columns — no SELECT *
rules.message: Avoid SELECT * — specify only the columns needed for better performance and schema-change resilience
rules.design_check: Does the design propose fetching all columns (SELECT *) for any query? If so, specify explicit column projections. Flag for discussion.

rules.description: Long-running queries must have a timeout configured
rules.message: Set statement_timeout or query timeout for long-running queries to avoid blocking connections in the pool
rules.design_check: Does the design include a statement timeout or query timeout for queries that could be long-running (reports, bulk exports, aggregations)? Flag if absent — unbounded queries can starve the pool.

transaction_discipline.description: Transaction scoping, isolation, and error handling rules

rules.description: Transactions must be short — no external I/O or heavy computation inside a transaction
rules.message: Keep transactions short — never place HTTP calls, file I/O, queue publishes, or heavy computation inside a DB transaction
rules.design_check: Does the design place HTTP calls, external service calls, file I/O, or heavy computation inside a database transaction? If so, move those operations outside the transaction boundary. BLOCK on long-running operations inside transactions.

rules.description: All transactions must handle errors and rollback explicitly
rules.message: Every transaction must have try/catch with explicit rollback — uncommitted transactions that error without rollback hold locks
rules.design_check: Does the design handle transaction rollback explicitly on error for all write operations? Flag if error handling is absent from any transaction flow.

rules.description: Nested transactions (savepoints mid-flow) must be avoided
rules.message: Avoid nested transactions — refactor into a single flat transaction boundary; use savepoints only when explicitly required
rules.design_check: Does the design call functions that start their own transactions from within an outer transaction? If so, flatten into a single transaction boundary. BLOCK on nested transaction proposals.

rules.description: Specify isolation level explicitly for write transactions with concurrency concerns
rules.message: For write transactions with concurrent access, specify isolation level (READ COMMITTED is default; use REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE when needed)
rules.design_check: Does the design involve concurrent writes to the same rows from multiple processes? If so, specify the required isolation level to prevent dirty reads, phantom reads, or lost updates.
